correctness.rationale: The switched graph is reconstructed exactly by an explicit bipartition, yielding part sizes \(b+x-y\) and \(a-x+y\). The identity condition follows from equality of unordered part-size pairs. Vandermonde's identity gives the exact selector count. The \(K_{2,3}\) nonclosure witness is a direct specialization. A standalone verifier independently checks every selector in 33 finite parameter cases, totaling 7,684 selectors.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For \(K_{2,3}\), the paper's own two example families supply \(S=\{b_1\}\) and \(T=\{a_1,b_1\}\) as identity switches. The exact switching calculation proves \(S\triangle T=\{a_1\}\) switches \(K_{2,3}\) to \(K_{1,4}\), so it is not an identity switch. This directly contradicts the stated subgroup claim rather than being a corollary of it.

The exact biclique classification explains precisely why the closure claim fails and supplies a reusable test family, rather than a one-off numerical counterexample.
